post.title: 529 plans: how they work, and what if kids skip college
post.ig:
What if your kid skips college? That 529 money isn't stuck.

Under federal law, 529 earnings grow tax-free and withdrawals for qualified education are tax-free; state deductions vary by state.
529 plans held about $603 billion ($602.9B) at the end of 2025 (ICI).
The One Big Beautiful Bill Act (July 2025) raised the K-12 limit from $10,000 to $20,000 a year starting in 2026.
Non-qualified withdrawals: earnings taxed plus a 10% penalty, with exceptions like scholarships. Under SECURE 2.0, up to $35,000 lifetime can roll to the beneficiary's Roth IRA if the 529 is 15+ years old, within annual IRA limits.
Example: $100/month for 18 years at an assumed 6% = $38,735 ($21,600 put in). Not a prediction.

Sources: IRS, ICI, One Big Beautiful Bill Act, SECURE 2.0 Act, Vanguard.
